image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket and short trousers, scuffed boots, stands small in a warm lush wood of still pools while Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, calm and majestic, stands in light and looks down at him

storyboard.claim: Aslan sends Digory on a quest west to the garden.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory standing small before the lion in the wood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the healing arc after the grief in London.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lion gives the task in person.

image.subject: a single silver apple resting on a mossy stone in green dappled light, a lush wood of still pools behind it

storyboard.claim: The apple will grow a tree that keeps the witch out of Narnia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: One silver apple on a mossy stone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the object of the quest.
storyboard.addedInformation: The apple's purpose is protection.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven in a grey wool jacket, rides on the back of Fledge, a strong chestnut horse with large feathered wings spread wide, flying over green hills under a bright sky

storyboard.claim: Digory flies on Fledge, the winged horse, to the garden.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy riding a winged chestnut horse over hills.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strawberry is now Fledge.

image.subject: a high wall of gold on a steep hill, with a tall gate facing east and a garden of overgrown sweet flowers and fruit trees glowing inside it

storyboard.claim: The garden is walled in gold with a gate facing east.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A golden wall on a steep hill with a gate.
storyboard.addedInformation: The garden is life-giving and sweet.

storyboard.claim: The gate carries a warning against stealing or climbing the wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Iron gate in a golden wall, the inscription cut into it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Digory reads the gate after arriving.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stealing or climbing brings despair.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven in a grey wool jacket, reaches up to a branch and lifts a silver apple, then slips it into his jacket pocket inside a walled golden garden

storyboard.claim: Digory takes the apple and pockets it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy's hand lifting an apple from a branch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: He ignores the warning on the gate.
storyboard.addedInformation: He has now broken the rule.

image.subject: Digory turns in a golden garden and sees Jadis, a tall, beautiful woman with black hair and a cold white face, a long dark gown with a silver crown, regal and terrifying, standing among the apple trees

storyboard.claim: Digory turns and finds Jadis in the garden.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy turning to see the tall witch under the trees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Digory is caught after taking the apple.
storyboard.addedInformation: Jadis has climbed the wall too.

image.subject: Jadis, a tall woman with black hair and a cold white face, a long dark gown and silver crown, holds a half-eaten silver apple with juice running down her chin inside a golden garden wall

storyboard.claim: Jadis has eaten an apple of her own.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Witch with juice on chin and a bitten apple.
storyboard.addedInformation: She has already climbed and eaten.

image.subject: close view of Jadis, a tall woman with black hair and a cold white face, skin drained to a dead white, a silver crown above her dark eyes, in the shadow of a golden garden wall

storyboard.claim: Eating the apple made her immortal but her skin turned dead white.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close view of the witch's dead-white face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of the apple.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her immortality is cursed.

image.subject: Jadis, a tall woman with black hair and a cold white face in a long dark gown, sits alone in the shadow of a golden garden wall, one hand resting on her knee, looking weary and trapped

storyboard.claim: The magic sustains her, but her life is cursed and miserable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis alone in shadow, weary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her immortality is a sentence, not a gift.

image.subject: Jadis leans close to Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven in a grey wool jacket, and points at his jacket pocket inside a golden garden, her cold white face bent toward him

storyboard.claim: Jadis tempts Digory to look at the apple in his pocket.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Witch leaning in, pointing at the pocket.
storyboard.addedInformation: She offers a use for the apple.

storyboard.claim: Jadis urges Digory to take the apple to London and save his mother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis's words set over a pocket and a London street.
storyboard.addedInformation: She offers the mother's life as the reason.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven in a grey wool jacket, stands alone at a stone crossroads in a lush wood, two paths splitting away from him in pale light

storyboard.claim: Digory stands at the same crossroads Uncle Andrew stood at.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy alone at a fork in the path.
storyboard.addedInformation: Digory faces the same choice.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, stands in a golden garden with his hand pressed against the pocket holding the silver apple, his face torn

storyboard.claim: Digory has the power to take something unearned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy's hand on his pocket, face torn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The desire is personal, not vain.

left.label: UNCLE ANDREW
left.subject: an old man, wild grey hair, a sharply pointed nose, a dressing gown over a waistcoat, pale vain face, Victorian scholar-magician, admiring himself in a dim study mirror

right.label: DIGORY
right.subject: a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket, kneeling by a bed where a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl lies weary

storyboard.claim: Digory's desire is more sympathetic than Uncle Andrew's ego.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vain old man beside a boy kneeling by a sick bed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Digory wants to save his mother.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, head bowed in a dim sickroom, his hand near a pale thin Edwardian woman lying in a white nightgown and shawl, frail and weary

storyboard.claim: Digory almost breaks, hearing his mother's voice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy's bowed head at the sickbed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sickroom is the source of the temptation.

image.subject: Jadis leans close to Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, while Polly Plummer, a girl of about eleven with dark plaited hair and a pinafore, stands apart in a golden garden looking worried

storyboard.claim: Jadis suggests Digory leave Polly behind so the lion would not know.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Witch whispering; Polly apart and worried.
storyboard.addedInformation: Polly is put at risk.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, turns sharply away from Jadis, a tall woman with black hair and a cold white face, his jaw set hard in a golden garden

storyboard.claim: Digory realizes Jadis does not understand loyalty, love or sacrifice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy turning sharply away from the witch.
storyboard.addedInformation: The witch is shown to lack love.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, walks away from a tall woman in a dark gown under golden garden trees, toward a chestnut horse with folded feathered wings waiting in the light

storyboard.claim: Digory walks away from the witch and flies back to Aslan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy walking away toward the waiting winged horse.
storyboard.addedInformation: He returns to Fledge.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, holds out a silver apple to Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, calm and majestic, standing in light

storyboard.claim: Digory hands the apple over to Aslan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy offering the apple to the lion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Next: the return to London.

image.subject: a young silver tree rising quickly from green ground under a new bright sky full of stars, in a newborn Narnian forest

storyboard.claim: The apple is planted and a magnificent silver tree grows rapidly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young silver tree under stars.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree will shelter Narnia.

image.subject: Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, stands in light beneath a silver tree in a newborn Narnian forest, a crown ready for a new king and queen

storyboard.claim: Aslan crowns the first king and queen of Narnia, and it is not Digory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lion beneath the silver tree with a crown.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crown goes to ordinary people.

image.subject: Frank the cabby, a weathered working-class London cabman, flat cap, heavy wool coat, thick moustache, kneels before a huge golden-tawny lion beneath a silver tree while his wife stands beside him

storyboard.claim: Aslan crowns Frank the cabby and his wife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cabman kneeling to be crowned.
storyboard.addedInformation: A London cabman becomes royalty.

image.subject: Frank the cabby, a weathered working-class London cabman, flat cap, heavy wool coat, thick moustache, rests his hand on the neck of a horse beneath a silver tree

storyboard.claim: Frank is a working man who loves his horse and is merciful and brave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cabman with hand on horse's neck.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mercy and bravery, not cunning.

image.subject: Frank the cabby and his wife Helen stand together under a young silver tree, both wearing thin silver crowns, calm faces, his flat cap resting on the grass

storyboard.claim: The cunning and exhaustion of London wash away; they are elevated to royalty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The cabbie and his wife stand crowned under the tree, calm and at peace.
storyboard.addedInformation: They serve the land rather than exploit it.

image.subject: a golden-tawny lion beneath a silver tree and a chestnut horse with folded wings, standing peacefully together in a bright new Narnian forest

storyboard.claim: The rulers serve the creatures rather than exploiting them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lion and winged horse in the new forest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Creatures are protected, not used.

storyboard.claim: Digory does the right thing, Frank gets crowned, and the tree grows perfectly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A silver tree grows over a crowned cabman and his wife while a boy in a grey jacket looks on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the critique.

storyboard.claim: Does the moral framework strain under its own neatness?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question on screen above the silver tree.
storyboard.addedInformation: Raises the question of the book's moral system.

image.subject: Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, calm and majestic, lowers his head to give Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, an apple from a silver tree in light

storyboard.claim: Aslan rewards Digory with an apple from the new tree to take to his mother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lion handing the boy an apple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the critique with the reward.
storyboard.addedInformation: Andrew and Jadis are punished.

storyboard.claim: Does it feel like a cosmic vending machine: obedience in, reward out?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question on screen beside a brass vending machine under a starry sky.
storyboard.addedInformation: A fair critique is raised.

storyboard.claim: Lewis skirts didacticism, but the system is more nuanced than simple reward.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator's line on screen beside an open book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Argues against a simple reward reading.

image.subject: Mrs Kirke, a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl, lies in a bed in a dim sickroom, looking toward a silver apple resting on the blanket

storyboard.claim: Aslan explains the stolen apple would have healed his mother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mother in bed with an apple on the blanket.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what the theft would have done.
storyboard.addedInformation: Healing was the stolen apple's promise.

storyboard.claim: She would have lived, and wished she had not, so the magic would have been corrupted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mrs Kirke alive in bed, turning her face away from an apple on the bedside table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of the theft.
storyboard.addedInformation: The theft corrupts the healing.

storyboard.claim: The means dictate the ends: a corrupted act yields a corrupted result.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The lesson set on screen over a pale sickroom wall.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lesson is not a prize for obedience.

storyboard.claim: Digory's reward is not the apple but the purity of the choice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory, a slim boy in a grey jacket, holds the silver apple at a sickroom doorway.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reward is inward.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, holds a silver apple in both hands, looking down at it in a warm lush wood of still pools

storyboard.claim: The healing will be pure because the choice to obtain it was pure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy holding the apple in both hands.
storyboard.addedInformation: The choice gives the healing its purity.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, and Polly Plummer, a girl of about eleven with dark plaited hair, raise yellow and green rings toward a still pool in a warm lush wood between the worlds

storyboard.claim: Digory and Polly say goodbye and plunge back through the wood to London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two children raising their rings over a pool.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rings carry them home.

image.subject: an old man, wild grey hair, a sharply pointed nose, a dressing gown over a waistcoat, pale vain face, sits alone in a dusty shattered London attic study beside a highback chair and a ticking clock, an empty red tray on the table

storyboard.claim: Uncle Andrew is left alone in his shattered study and never touches magic again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Old man alone in the wrecked study.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magic is gone from his life.

image.subject: an old man, wild grey hair, a sharply pointed nose, a dressing gown over a waistcoat, pale vain face, leans on a dim pub table with a glass in his hand, boasting to two listeners who lean in

storyboard.claim: Andrew spends his old age drinking and boasting to anyone who will listen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Old man boasting at a pub table.
storyboard.addedInformation: He spends his life retelling the story.

storyboard.claim: He brushed against the majesty of creation and reduced it to a barroom anecdote.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Uncle Andrew at a barroom counter, glass raised, telling his story to a listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sums up his wasted encounter.

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven in a grey wool jacket and scuffed boots, runs up a dim Edwardian staircase toward a half-open sickroom door, a gaslit hall below

storyboard.claim: But Digory rushes upstairs to his mother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boy running up the staircase.
storyboard.addedInformation: Leads into the healing.
